brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Four hex bases: full piece at (0,0), full at (0,1), full at (1,0), and a north half-base at (0,-1) (piece:0,-1,0;half-n), forming a compact cluster. check_build meshClash clear.
drawer:0#0,-1#cut (classic/stem s) on the cut face of the half-n base at (0,-1). Mesh clear against the bases.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 at the junction of cells (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), set to the mount variant (solid variant refused a platform).
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm applied to the mount spike at junction (0,0)/(0,1)/(1,0).

requirements.requirement: House rules: cap open faces and lock joints
requirements.evidence: lockJoints applied (3 joint bolts; LOOSE_BODY warning cleared). capOpenFaces refused with MESH_CLASH: cap hex-cap-edge-solid-m would run into hex-drawer-frame-s by 4.49 mm, and skipping the drawer face did not help, so the open faces are left uncapped (15 faces reported as open, info only).

finish.summary: Built a compact desk unit: four hex bases (three full and one north half) with a drawer on the half base's cut face, and a mount-type spike at the corner where three bases meet, carrying a small platform accessory. lockJoints is applied and check_build reports meshClash clear with no errors. The configurator would not cap the open faces because a cap collides with the drawer frame, so those faces remain open. No props were added since the brief did not ask for them.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
